Hi Diego / Sreeni,

Thanks again for the time today — good to meet the FinEdge infra team. Quick recap and the open network items we promised to capture so you have a single checklist:

- FinEdge stated preference: Private VPC (data residency + compliance) but evaluating PrivateLink vs VPC peering for connectivity to Redwood Private.
- Primary asks from the call:
  * Which connection pattern do you want: PrivateLink (managed ENIs) or VPC peering?
  * Egress / allowlist: will you manage a strict IP allowlist? How many IPs/blocks can you support?
  * Required ports and TLS termination expectations.
  * Who will own the peering/PrivateLink setup (FinEdge infra vs cloud ops partner)?
  * Timeline: you mentioned aiming for pilot by end of September.

Action items we committed to:
- Lauren: provide a concise port/CIDR checklist and preferred setup recommendations.
- Monica: share the Private VPC deployment checklist + any compliance notes.
- Rishi: follow up with a single thread + links to our hubspot record and templates.

I've attached our Redwood Private VPC checklist (redwood_private_vpc_checklist.pdf) for your review — it's intentionally short and highlights the minimal network info we need to spin up a test endpoint.

Next step: if you can reply with the items below we'll triage and schedule a 30–45m network preflight with your infra team and Lauren:
- AWS account IDs and primary VPC CIDR (or on-prem network if hybrid).
- Whether PrivateLink is preferred, or if peering is a hard requirement.
- Any existing egress IP allowlist limits (max number of IPs/blocks).
- Cloud region preference (you mentioned us-east-1).

Thanks — I'll hold on scheduling until I hear back on the above.

Best,

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode evaluation — Private VPC networking questions

Diego / team — quick technical follow-up, copying Monica for compliance context. Short checklist and clarifying questions so the preflight is focused:

1) Connection model: PrivateLink vs Peering
   - PrivateLink (recommended when customers want zero route overlap and simpler customer firewall rules). Requires you to create an endpoint service/accept an endpoint; traffic goes over AWS private ENIs.
   - VPC peering (recommended when you need full-routed access between subnets and lower per-GB egress costs sometimes). Peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route table changes.

2) Minimum network information we need to provision a test endpoint (please provide):
   - Account ID(s) and VPC ID(s) + primary CIDR(s)
   - List of permissable egress IPs/blocks (if you maintain an allowlist); if you have a strict 4-IP limit, tell us now.
   - Preferred TLS model: do you want Redwood to terminate TLS at our side (managed) or will FinEdge present a client cert / mTLS?

3) Ports and protocols (our runtime needs):
   - Outbound: TCP 443 (HTTPS) outbound from your VPC to our endpoint (default).
   - For peering: allow ephemeral high ports for mutual connections (we can lock to 443 if using PrivateLink).

4) IP addressing notes:
   - If using PrivateLink we present specific endpoint IPs in your subnets. For peering we will send traffic from our service CIDRs — we will provide them but prefer PrivateLink for tighter allowlisting.

5) Routing and NAT: confirm whether your subnets are private with NAT egress or have direct internet egress — that changes recommended testing steps.

I'll prepare a 2-slide network preflight template to use on the call. If you can answer above, I'll propose 2–3 times for the preflight.

-lb
Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi / Lauren — answered inline below and attaching a network diagram + a quick PrivateLink spreadsheet we keep for vendor onboarding.

On Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 11:18 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Connection model: PrivateLink vs Peering

We prefer PrivateLink for the initial pilot — avoids route table changes and fits our security posture. If PrivateLink proves costly for production scale we may reconsider peering.

> 2) Minimum network information we need to provision a test endpoint (please provide):

- AWS account ID: 123456789012
- Primary VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
- Primary CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16
- Egress allowlist constraints: we can accept up to 8 distinct IPs in our perimeter firewall.
- TLS model: we would like Redwood to terminate TLS (simpler for us), but we can evaluate mTLS for production.

> 3) Ports and protocols

Confirmed: outbound TCP 443 from VPC to endpoint. We will not allow arbitrary ephemeral ports in our perimeter; prefer PrivateLink so we can keep tighter rules.

> 4) IP addressing notes

Under PrivateLink we will accept ENIs in two private subnets.

> 5) Routing and NAT

Our subnets are private with NAT egress for some workloads, but we can arrange a dedicated private subnet for the Redwood endpoint if needed.

Attachments: finedge_network_diagram.png (diagram, internal only), finedge_privatelink_config.xlsx (spreadsheet with suggested subnet IDs and contacts).

Timeline: target pilot end of September remains accurate.

One operational ask: who on Redwood side will be the single point of contact for the network preflight? Also can you confirm whether Redwood requires inbound firewall rules from our side or only acceptance of the PrivateLink endpoint?

Thanks,
Diego
Director, Cloud Infrastructure | FinEdge
